Items and Gold: How to Shop

Where gold comes from, what to buy first, how items are built from parts, and when to go back to shop.

Where gold comes from

  • Minions: 14 to 50+ gold each, but only with the last hit. See Last-Hitting 101.
  • Champion kills: 300 gold at levels 1-6, rising to 420 at level 18. The first kill of the game (First Blood) gives +100 extra. Assists give a share too.
  • Towers and plates: every outer tower plate gives 120 gold early on. The first tower of the game gives +300 bonus gold.
  • Jungle camps and epic monsters: mostly for the jungler, but dragons and Baron give gold too.
  • Passive income: everyone gets a small amount of gold every second.

Starting items

You start with 500 gold. Most players buy a starter item and a Health Potion or two:

  • Doran's Ring: for mages. Ability power, health, and mana back when you damage enemies.
  • Doran's Blade: for fighters and some marksmen. Attack damage, health and healing.
  • Doran's Shield: for tanky laners in hard matchups. Health and regeneration.
  • Doran's Bow: a starter for marksmen who attack a lot.
  • World Atlas: the support item. Supports buy this instead.
  • Junglers buy a jungle pet, like Scorchclaw Pup or Gustwalker Hatchling, and need Smite.

How items are built

Big items (called legendary items) cost about 2,500 to 3,500 gold. You don't buy them all at once. Each one is built from cheaper components. For example, Rabadon's Deathcap is built from Needlessly Large Rod pieces.

When you go back to base with 1,200 gold, buy the most useful component of your next item. The stats help you right away, and you finish the full item later.

You can carry six items plus a trinket (a free ward item). Boots take one slot: everyone should buy them within the first few recalls.

Pro tipNot sure what to buy? Open the shop and use the Recommended tab. It shows good items for your champion. Our champion guides also list full builds for the current patch.

When to go back and shop

Pressing B starts your recall: after a few seconds you teleport to base, where you heal fully and can shop. Good times to recall:

  • You're low on health or mana and can't fight anymore.
  • You have enough gold for an important component (often around 1,100 to 1,300 gold).
  • You just pushed your minion wave into the enemy tower, so you won't miss much farm while you're gone.

Learn more about timing in Recall Timing and Tempo.

Common mistakeSitting on 3,000 unspent gold. Gold in your pocket does nothing. If you have a lot of gold and the game is quiet, go back and turn it into items.

Armor or magic resist?

Damage comes in three types:

  • Physical damage: from attacks and AD (attack damage) champions like marksmen and fighters. Armor reduces it.
  • Magic damage: from AP (ability power) champions like mages. Magic resist (MR) reduces it.
  • True damage: ignores both.

If the enemy laner or the fed enemy deals physical damage, defensive items with armor (like Plated Steelcaps or Zhonya's Hourglass for mages) help a lot. Against magic damage, buy MR (like Mercury's Treads or Banshee's Veil). Hover over an enemy's items with Tab to see what they built.

Reading item stats

Common stats you'll see: AD (attack damage), AP (ability power), attack speed, critical strike chance, ability haste (shorter cooldowns), health, armor, MR and lethality / magic penetration (ignore part of the enemy's defenses). Buy the stats your champion's abilities use: hover over an ability to see if it scales with AD or AP.

Key takeaways

  • Minions are your steadiest gold; kills and tower plates give big bursts.
  • Start with a Doran's item and a potion (or World Atlas as support, a pet as jungler).
  • Build big items from components each time you recall; buy boots early.
  • Recall when you're low, when you can afford a key part, or after pushing your wave.
  • Armor stops physical damage, magic resist stops magic damage.
